turns.assessment: The simultaneous failure of many services and OTU frames at S04/S14, while receive power, OSNR, amplifier telemetry, and channel-monitor power remained unchanged, indicates a digital payload interruption rather than loss of optical carriers. The affected set converges on traffic switched through S15, including services on different optical degrees; this is characteristic of the S15 OTN switch fabric failing. The post-LOF DGD and pre-FEC jumps are likely invalid/saturated receiver estimates after framing was lost, not evidence of a fibre DGD event.

proposals.rationale: A switch-fabric failure at S15 interrupts many ODUs simultaneously while leaving optical carriers, power, OSNR, and amplifier telemetry unchanged. It accounts for the broad service failures and protection events across multiple optical degrees at the same onset.
proposals.note: site named; resolved to its node equipment

proposals.rationale: S04 is common to many affected working routes and could create payload-only interruption, but services routed directly between S14 and S15 were also affected, making S04 substantially less likely.

proposals.rationale: A failed S15 WSS port could affect many channels, but it should cause optical signal or channel-power loss on one degree. Unchanged optical measurements and impacts spanning different degrees argue strongly against it.
